items.title: MR-Guided Single-Fraction Radiation for Oligorecurrent Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tests whether one high-dose radiation treatment can safely treat prostate cancer that has returned in a few lymph nodes after initial curative treatment. It uses MRI guidance during treatment to precisely target tumors. The study will enroll 48 patients and measure safety, tumor control, and time before hormone therapy is needed.

items.title: Exercise Training Effects on Quality of Life in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This study examines how structured strength and endurance training affects quality of life, fitness, and survival in prostate cancer patients. Exercise may help counter common side effects like fatigue, muscle loss, and depression, especially from androgen deprivation therapy. The trial is no longer recruiting patients.

items.title: AZD6621 Trial for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 study tests the experimental drug AZD6621 in men with metastatic prostate cancer. The study has two parts: Part A finds the safest dose, and Part B tests effectiveness in more patients. The trial is actively recruiting and will test different delivery methods.

items.title: Opevesostat vs Standard Hormone Therapy in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares opevesostat (a novel hormonal agent) to switching between standard hormone drugs (abiraterone or enzalutamide) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients who already tried one hormone therapy. The study tests whether opevesostat can delay cancer progression better than switching to another standard drug. Actively recruiting.

items.title: Adding Docetaxel to Hormone Therapy for Suboptimal PSA Response
items.summary: This phase 3 trial studies whether adding docetaxel chemotherapy to standard hormone treatment helps patients with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer whose PSA levels haven't responded well. The trial compares this combination to continuing hormone therapy alone. Actively recruiting.

items.title: Radioactive PSMA Therapy Plus Olaparib for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 2 study combines FPI-2265 (a radioactive drug targeting PSMA) with olaparib (a PARP inhibitor) for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The radioactive treatment delivers targeted radiation to cancer cells, while olaparib blocks DNA repair. The trial is testing different dosing schedules but not currently recruiting.

items.title: QLF4113 Phase 1 Trial for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This early-phase trial tests the experimental drug QLF4113 in men with metastatic prostate cancer. The study has two parts: finding the right dose and then testing effectiveness at that dose. It will measure safety, how the drug moves through the body, and early signs of cancer response. Not yet recruiting.

items.title: Shorter Radiation Course for Recurrent Oligometastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial studies whether a shorter course of radiation therapy (either proton beam or IMRT) is effective with fewer side effects for men whose prostate cancer has returned or spread to a limited number of sites. The study is no longer recruiting and focuses on safety and tumor control.

items.title: Tulmimetostat Combined with Hormone Therapy for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 study tests tulmimetostat (an experimental epigenetic drug) combined with either darolutamide or abiraterone in men with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. The trial evaluates safety and effectiveness of these new combinations. Actively recruiting.

items.title: New PET Imaging Agent Compared to Standard PSMA Scan
items.summary: This phase 2 trial compares a new investigational PET imaging agent (61Cu-NU101) to the standard Pylarify scan for detecting prostate cancer spread. The study will enroll 34 patients and test whether the new imaging method is as good or better at finding metastases. Not yet recruiting.

items.title: HER2-Targeted Therapy Plus Enzalutamide for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This completed phase 2 trial tested whether adding HER2-targeted antibodies (pertuzumab and trastuzumab) to enzalutamide could treat metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. HER2 is a protein found on some cancer cells, and blocking it may help stop tumor growth. The study has finished enrollment.

items.title: Cabozantinib Plus Lutetium-177 PSMA for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 1b trial combines cabozantinib with lutetium-177 PSMA-617 radioactive therapy for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is finding the safest dose combination and is currently paused. It aims to improve the effectiveness of radioactive PSMA treatment.

items.title: Actinium-225 PSMA Plus Hormone Therapy for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares actinium-225 PSMA radioactive therapy plus hormone treatment to standard care (hormone switch, chemotherapy, or lutetium-177 PSMA) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients who progressed on one hormone therapy. Actinium-225 delivers stronger radiation than lutetium-177. Actively recruiting.

items.title: Blood Collection Study to Identify Genetic Factors in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This observational study collects blood samples from prostate cancer patients to identify gene differences that may explain why some cancers become resistant to hormone therapy. The study aims to understand the genetic factors behind aggressive disease progression. Actively recruiting.

items.title: QLC5508 vs Docetaxel in Metastatic CRPC After Hormone Therapy
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares the experimental drug QLC5508 to standard docetaxel chemotherapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients who progressed after hormone therapy. The study measures how long patients live without cancer progression. Not yet recruiting.

items.title: Radium-223 vs Hormone Therapy Switch for Bone Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 4 trial compares radium-223 radioactive treatment to switching hormone therapy (abiraterone or enzalutamide) in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer that has spread to bones. Radium-223 targets bone metastases specifically. No longer recruiting.

items.title: Niraparib Combinations for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 study tests niraparib (a PARP inhibitor) combined with other drugs for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The trial aims to find the right dose and evaluate effectiveness and safety of these combinations. No longer recruiting new patients.

items.title: Lutetium-177 PSMA Safety and Effectiveness Study in Chinese Patients
items.summary: This completed phase 2 study evaluated lutetium-177 PSMA-617 radioactive therapy in Chinese men with progressive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who had prior hormone therapy and chemotherapy. The study assessed safety, effectiveness, and how the drug moves through the body to support regulatory approval in China.

items.title: Lutetium-177 PSMA Plus Standard Care for Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This large phase 3 trial compares lutetium-177 PSMA-617 radioactive therapy combined with standard hormone treatment to standard hormone treatment alone in men with newly metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. The study enrolled over 1,100 patients worldwide and is no longer recruiting. Results could establish earlier use of PSMA therapy.

items.title: JNJ-78278343 T-Cell Therapy for Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 study tested JNJ-78278343, an experimental treatment that redirects the immune system's T-cells to attack prostate cancer cells by targeting a protein called KLK2. The trial found the recommended dose and evaluated safety. No longer recruiting.

items.title: Pasritamig Combination Therapy for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 study tests pasritamig (an immune-redirecting therapy) combined with other drugs for metastatic prostate cancer. The trial is finding safe doses of these combinations and then testing effectiveness. Actively recruiting patients.

items.title: AB-3028 CAR-T Cell Therapy for Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial evaluates AB-3028, an engineered T-cell therapy (CAR-T) designed to target metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study tests safety and effectiveness of this novel immune therapy approach. Actively recruiting.

items.title: Niraparib Plus Abiraterone for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares niraparib (a PARP inhibitor) combined with abiraterone hormone therapy to abiraterone alone in men with metastatic prostate cancer. The study evaluates whether adding niraparib improves outcomes. No longer recruiting.

items.title: Apalutamide for Non-Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial evaluated apalutamide in men with high-risk non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (cancer that no longer responds to hormone therapy but hasn't spread yet). The study is no longer recruiting and assessed whether the drug delays spread of cancer.

items.title: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 study tests whether adding mevrometostat (PF-06821497, an epigenetic drug) to enzalutamide works better than enzalutamide alone in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who haven't had prior enzalutamide or abiraterone. Actively recruiting.

items.title: Niraparib Plus Abiraterone for DNA Repair Gene Mutation Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial tested niraparib (PARP inhibitor) combined with abiraterone in men with newly metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer who have mutations in DNA repair genes (HRR genes). These mutations make tumors more sensitive to PARP inhibitors. No longer recruiting.

items.title: Apalutamide Plus Abiraterone for Metastatic CRPC Without Prior Chemotherapy
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compared combining two hormone therapies (apalutamide plus abiraterone) to abiraterone alone in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients who hadn't received chemotherapy yet. The study evaluated whether the double hormone therapy combination delays cancer progression. No longer recruiting.

items.title: Ferroptosis as Novel Treatment Target in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This research review explains ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of cell death, as a promising new treatment approach for castration-resistant prostate cancer. The review discusses how inducing ferroptosis can overcome drug resistance and work synergistically with existing therapies like hormone treatment and chemotherapy. It outlines the molecular pathways involved and proposes a framework for developing combination treatments.

items.title: Nanotechnology Treatment Overcomes Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer Resistance
items.summary: This preclinical study developed an injectable gel that delivers enzymes generating reactive oxygen species and a drug blocking cell recycling systems. The combination approach overcomes resistance mechanisms in castration-resistant prostate cancer by causing oxidative damage while preventing cancer cells from repairing themselves. This is laboratory research not yet tested in humans.

items.title: Dual BRD4/AKT Inhibitor Overcomes c-MYC Resistance in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This laboratory study identified a new compound that simultaneously blocks two pathways (BRD4 and AKT) that drive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The dual-target approach overcomes resistance caused by c-MYC, a cancer-promoting gene that becomes elevated when AKT inhibitors are used alone. This is early-stage drug development research.

items.title: Chinese Herbal Medicine Delays Enzalutamide Resistance in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This preclinical study found that a traditional Chinese herbal formula (GBQY) combined with enzalutamide helps delay drug resistance in castration-resistant prostate cancer. The herbs work by reducing tumor oxygen deprivation and altering cancer stem cell metabolism. This research used cell and animal models, not human trials.

items.title: Building Sustainable Theranostics Programs for Cancer Treatment
items.summary: This review discusses how to establish sustainable programs for theranostics—treatments that combine imaging and targeted radioactive therapy like lutetium-177 PSMA for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. It covers operational requirements including facilities, trained staff, radiation safety, supply chain, and reimbursement needed to deliver these therapies safely and equitably.

items.title: Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors Efficacy Meta-Analysis for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This meta-analysis combined data from 21 trials involving 1,580 metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors. Overall survival at one year was 63% and at two years was 39%. Combining immune therapy with other drugs showed better results than immune therapy alone, though benefits were modest in unselected patients.

items.title: PIM1 Kinase Promotes Drug Resistance Through Cell Survival Pathway
items.summary: This research identifies how the PIM1 protein helps castration-resistant prostate cancer resist treatment by activating cell survival mechanisms that reduce oxidative stress. Standard drugs that block PIM1's enzyme activity actually increase total PIM1 protein, limiting effectiveness. A new type of drug (PROTAC) that destroys PIM1 protein shows promise in overcoming this resistance.

items.title: Diabetes Drug Canagliflozin Blocks Androgen Receptor in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This laboratory study found that canagliflozin, an FDA-approved diabetes medication, directly inhibits androgen receptor signaling in prostate cancer, including resistant AR-V7 variants. The drug works through a different mechanism than standard hormone therapies, suggesting it could be repurposed to treat both castration-sensitive and castration-resistant prostate cancer. This is preclinical research.

items.title: Targeting Regulatory T Cells in Prostate Cancer Microenvironment
items.summary: This review examines how regulatory T cells (Tregs) in the tumor environment help prostate cancer evade the immune system. The spatial distribution and activation state of Tregs, rather than just their numbers, predict aggressive disease. The review discusses current and emerging therapies targeting Tregs, including antibodies and combination strategies with immunotherapy.

items.title: GLUL Enzyme Drives Docetaxel Resistance Through Metabolic Changes
items.summary: This research identified the GLUL enzyme, which produces glutamine, as a key driver of docetaxel chemotherapy resistance in castration-resistant prostate cancer. High GLUL levels correlate with activated growth signaling pathways and metabolic changes that help cancer cells survive treatment. This finding suggests GLUL as a potential therapeutic target to overcome chemotherapy resistance.

items.title: Ailanthone Suppresses Blood Vessel Mimicry in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This preclinical study found that ailanthone, a natural compound, blocks prostate cancer cells from forming their own blood vessel-like structures (vasculogenic mimicry), which contributes to aggressive disease. The compound works by altering gene regulation that controls cell signaling pathways. Animal studies showed reduced tumor growth and blood vessel formation.
